svg.aria-label: The dense crowd image. Left: six frame properties — heads are tiny and perspective spans a large scale range; occlusion is the norm so only heads are visible; labels are one dot per head; most of the image is empty; counts are long-tailed; the dangerous number is people per square metre. Right: six output layers from L0 scene geometry, L1 count and density map, L2 head points, L3 boxes and instance masks, L4 unique counts across time and views, to L5 risk and semantics, with example 2025-26 methods for each.
svg.title: The dense crowd image: six properties, six output layers
svg.text: The dense crowd image: what makes it different, and what we ask of it
Left: properties of the frame. Right: output layers, cheapest at the bottom. Each layer above L1 needs more labels and fails earlier as density rises.

g.text: 1 · Heads are tiny, and scale varies with depth
A few pixels at the back, hundreds at the front of one frame
2 · Occlusion is the norm
Bodies are hidden; often only a head or hair is visible
3 · Labels are dots
One point per head, hundreds to thousands per image
4 · Most of the image is empty
ZIP reports >95 % of blocks contain nobody
5 · Counts are long-tailed
0 to >10,000 per image; error grows with density
6 · The dangerous number is per m², not per image
Contact at ~5–6 p/m², collapse risk at ~8–10 p/m²
L5 · Risk and semantics
Crowd Pressure Index from CCTV; VLM answers (CrowdCue, UNICBench)
L4 · Unique people across time and views
Video individual counting: OMAN++, GD3A/DVTrack; multi-view fusion
L3 · Boxes and instance masks
DGA + DG-NMS; YOLO26 + Second-Look head; XMask / EDP-SAM
L2 · Head points (localisation)
P2PNet lineage; P2R loss; Consistent-Point (semi-supervised)
L1 · Count and density map
ZIP (zero-inflated Poisson); DCA-MoE on frozen DINOv3; L2HCount
L0 · Scene geometry
Perspective / scale map, region of interest, pixels → m² calibration

svg.text: Blue: perception layers. Orange: decision layers. Grey: geometry that turns counts into densities per m². Thresholds from the ICACT 2026 CPI paper.
